_comment: RE-PINNED 2026-11-25 to redevops-projects release v0.3.9 (commit 5ad1ebbc: an unavailable dashboard says why it is not shown, what it needs and how to enable it). The build output is byte-identical, file by file, to the published release asset projects-ui-root.tgz of v0.3.9 (sha256 71328177a5340edea0dc4a48421221024e9306407b877c522451a3a216e7083c), which additionally carries hero.jpg. Previous pins are kept below (pin_33c1a3e0, pin_e6032e8e, pin_2bbb9811). Earlier note: RE-PINNED 2026-11-25 to redevops-projects release v0.3.2 (commit 33c1a3e0: the Dashboards section, Sidekick docked beside the page, no demo content on a deployment that serves no fixtures). The build output is byte-identical, file by file, to the published release asset projects-ui-root.tgz of v0.3.2 (sha256 13f9be92479ef9b2471e97788847792e39ddf73d27b15ed02f5196aa59cb9a74), which additionally carries hero.jpg. RE-PINNED 2026-11-24 to redevops-projects main e6032e8e (PRs #28 and #29 on top of 2bbb9811: Today honours a read-only deployment; every flexible grid track can shrink, which fixes the page being wider than a 390 px window on Linux). The pinned Projects UI artifact: url + sha256 + source commit. RE-PINNED 2026-11-19 (owner decision): the previous pin's source commit (ea9e53e56b...24fa, and its whole ancestor chain back through 9a1788b1, 5751e9e5, 312a811a, 2f24719e, ee958a01, 2fdef7f5) was a LOCAL, UNPUBLISHED commit of a local redevops-projects clone; that clone was lost in the 2026-11-07 scratchpad wipe and no longer exists anywhere (checked: no surviving local clone, no dangling git object by that sha in any repository on this machine, no remote branch/tag). Only the already-built, minified dist output of that lost source survives, in the `previous_pin` chain below, as history. This build is therefore pinned instead to the current public tip of github.com/redevops-io/redevops-projects's `main` branch (source_commit, below), which is itself two commits past the v0.2.0 release (base_commit) this repository had previously built on. Because source_commit is a real commit on the public repository's default branch today, source_commit_published is TRUE: decisions pins-04 and pins-10 (packaging/DECISIONS-REQUIRED.md, packaging/PINS.md) are resolved by this fact alone. D-LIC-12 (which AGPL section 6 option to use for the Corresponding Source) stays OPEN and is NOT decided by this re-pin -- that remains the owner's/counsel's choice among options (a)-(d); this re-pin only makes options (a) and (c) actually available, where before only a repository pointer to unpublished work could be offered. Known regression: this re-pin DROPS every feature that only existed in the lost local commits -- the accessibility series (UIA-01..12), the mission drill-down views, the data-source-driven 'Partly sample' chip, and the fixed-wording connect/propose/remove-source flows. None of that is in this build; it ships only what is on the public repository today (the Today-first views of v0.2.0 plus PR #24 routing/restore-last-place, #25 audit-findings fixes, #26 Snooze-on-live-signals). Redoing and this time actually pushing that lost work is tracked separately, not by this lock file. scripts/fetch_projects_ui.py verifies the sha256 before anything is extracted, whichever source it reads. `previous_pin` is the artifact this one replaces (the previous, now-unrecoverable-source local build chain), which stays in the repository: going back is a lock edit.

merged_public_release.note: v0.2.0 is an ancestor of source_commit on the public repository's own main branch (PRs #24, #25, #26 are the commits between them); nothing is merged in from a lost local branch anymore, source_commit IS the public history.

recipe.reproduced: index.html, the JavaScript and the CSS were built three times from a clean `git archive` of source_commit, each in its own throwaway HOME, TMPDIR and npm cache under env -i (node v24.22.3, npm 11.19.1, npm ci), on 2026-11-19, with identical sha256 each time; three consecutive packs give an identical archive.

previous_pin._comment: The pinned Projects UI artifact: url + sha256 + source commit. TODAY the artifact is built LOCALLY from an UNPUBLISHED commit of the UI source (source_commit_published=false) and lives in this repository (local_path), so builds and tests are offline and reproducible; no release of redevops-projects has been published for it, so `url` is empty and this record is NOT a source offer (decisions pins-04, pins-10 and D-LIC-12 stay OPEN; packaging/ui-bundle-source.json carries the same provenance). The source commit MERGES the public release v0.2.0 (Today-first views: Today, capture, batch triage, notifications, routing, deployment-inspection and social-intelligence cards) into the local accessibility series (UIA-01..12) and adds the mission drill-down views (Summary, Tasks, Evidence with Inspect, Timeline, Graph, World State, EXPLAIN, Replay). The Sample chip and every sample-versus-recorded decision come from what the RUNNING SERVER reports (GET /api/ui-config), not from a build flag: this one artifact serves a sample deployment and a runtime-backed one. When the server says runtime but the provider-backed pages (Missions list, Overview, Today) are still the sample projection, the top bar shows a "Partly sample" chip with a keyboard-reachable explanation, decided from the same report. `previous_pin` is the artifact this one replaces (the previous local build, whose Sample chip was a build flag; its own previous_pin chain goes back through the accessibility series to the public v0.2.0), which stays in the repository: going back is a lock edit. scripts/fetch_projects_ui.py verifies the sha256 before anything is extracted, whichever source it reads. The mission views also flag, in words and a glyph with the cites of the events, a step whose outcome is unknown, a late (stale) result and a compensation that did not complete cleanly, show the mission state in plain words (the raw state kept), and list independent read-backs as evidence with the verifier kind as recorded. Keyboard focus is visible on every focusable element from one shared :focus-visible ring (a --focus token, a system colour in forced-colors mode). Connecting, proposing and removing a source never fail silently: every refusal and failure of Connect & scan, Looks right and Remove is said in the page's own fixed sentences, keyed by the server's refusal code (the server's own message text is never shown), with the folder named as plain text; a folder registered in this session has a Remove button with an in-page question.

merged_public_release.note: public release of redevops-projects, merged into the source commit; not an ancestor of the accessibility series base

The archive bytes also depend on the zlib in use; the member hashes above are the portable invariant, the archive sha256 is what is pinned.

the same views before connecting, proposing and removing a source said anything when refused: a refused Connect & scan or Looks right rejected inside the page and showed nothing (the form stayed as typed, no message), and a folder registered in a session had no Remove button. Kept in the repository so that reverting is a lock edit.

the same views before the keyboard-focus fix: the top-bar 'Ask Sidekick' input had an inline `outline: none` and no focus indicator (WCAG 2.4.7; found by the native accessibility harness, rows A11Y-FOCUS and A11Y-FOCUS-FORCED), and a focused control in a sideways-scrolling table could have its ring cut at 320 px. Kept in the repository so that reverting is a lock edit.

the same views with the 'Partly sample' chip, before the drill-down flags for an uncertain step, a late (stale) result and a compensation that did not complete cleanly, the plain-words mission state, and the read-back evidence rows. Kept in the repository so that reverting is a lock edit.

the same views and the same data-source report, with a Sample chip that was either on (sample) or off (runtime) and so said nothing about provider-backed pages that are still sample in a runtime deployment. Kept in the repository so that reverting is a lock edit.

Today-first views + accessibility series (UIA-01..12) + the read-only mission drill-down, with the Sample chip and every sample-versus-recorded decision taken from a BUILD FLAG (VITE_PROJECTS_SAMPLE_DATA, default on): one artifact could not serve a runtime-backed deployment without a second build. Kept in the repository so that reverting is a lock edit.

the accessibility series (UIA-01..12) on the old public base 5114b560 only: it does NOT contain the Today-first views and has one shared body for every mission tab. Kept in the repository so that reverting is a lock edit.

public release asset fetched by origin/main; Today-first UI (Today, capture, batch triage, notifications, routing, deployment-inspection and social-intelligence cards). The accessibility series (UIA-01..12) is NOT in it and the Today-first views are NOT in the current artifact.
